subject: Pilot runway adjustment & usage safeguard — ClearHarbor POC
messages:
From: Emma Lewis <emma@clearharbor.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@clearharbor.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC timeline and usage spike — request to extend runway

Hi Dylan,

Quick note from our side — thanks again for the help getting the ClearHarbor pilot live. We started a larger internal test yesterday and saw an unexpected usage spike that will push us past the current 30-day evaluation runway by next week.

Two asks:
- Could we get a short, two-week extension on the pilot while we finish the last set of integration tests?
- If an extension isn’t possible, would Redwood consider a one-time credit we can consume during the spike so our team can validate the higher-throughput workload?

I attached our usage export so you can see the shape of the spike (clearharbor-usage-2026-02.csv). We’re not looking to change pricing yet — just trying to avoid throttling while we prove the final flows.

If helpful I can share a short note from our engineering lead explaining the test plan.

Thanks — Emma

-- 
Emma Lewis
Director of ML Integrations | ClearHarbor
emma@clearharbor.ai
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lewis <emma@clearharbor.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@clearharbor.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Feb 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC timeline and usage spike — request to extend runway

Thanks for the data, Emma — looks like a clean spike and good signal. We can absolutely help avoid noisy throttles while you validate. Two pragmatic paths we typically offer for these cases:

Option 1 — Timebox extension: add 14 calendar days to the current trial window. No extra charge if you agree to a pilot-to-paid decision point within 30 days after the extension.

Option 2 — Usage credit: issue a one-time usage credit you can draw down during the spike. Credits are applied to invoices or to the pilot bucket (your preference).

For transparency I’m attaching a short proposal with the ranges we see for similar spikes (proposed-concessions.xlsx). Before I lock anything down I’m looping in Monica (solutions) and Neha (pricing) to confirm the finance side and the technical guardrails.

If you have a preference today, tell me A or B and we’ll draft the exact terms.

Best,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Emma Lewis <emma@clearharbor.ai>, Raj Patel <raj@clearharbor.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Feb 2026 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC timeline and usage spike — request to extend runway

Looping in pricing/finance details here. Dylan — thanks for the quick note. We can support both approaches but need to lock a few conditions so this stays clean from a billing and audit perspective. Proposed terms: 

- Timebox extension (Option 1): 14 days added to the existing pilot effective immediately. No charge provided ClearHarbor executes a signed SOW (based on our standard template) within 30 days of the extension end date. Any usage > 3x baseline during the extension is billed at a mitigated overage rate of $0.045/1K tokens to prevent runaway cost; we will cap overall overage billing to $5k for the extension period.

- Usage credit (Option 2): Issue a $15,000 usage credit that can be consumed during the spike. Credit is applied to the first paid invoice once a purchase order (or signed SOW) is received within 60 days. Unused credit expires after 90 days.

- Common requirements: attach the SOW template below, require PO or signed SOW to convert credits to invoice credits. Credits are non-transferable.

Attached: sow-template.docx. If you’d like, we can draft a short amendment now so you don’t need to wait for a full PO.

Neha
Finance & Pricing Operations | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
From: Emma Lewis <emma@clearharbor.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@clearharbor.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Feb 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC timeline and usage spike — request to extend runway

Appreciate the clear options. A few clarifying asks before we pick: 

1) For Option 1, does the overage cap ($5k) come out of our pocket during the extension, or would Redwood absorb any overage beyond the cap if we stay on track for a conversion?
2) For Option 2, can the $15k credit be applied directly to the pilot (so it prevents throttling immediately) and then be reconciled on the first invoice? We want to avoid a PO right now if possible.
3) We also need a short written confirmation that extending the pilot won’t change data retention policies or access controls for our trial data — that’s a compliance ask from our security team.

If we can get short answers to these three points, I think we can pick today.

Thanks — Emma
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lewis <emma@clearharbor.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC timeline and usage spike — request to extend runway

Hi Emma — quick note from CS/solutions perspective. Two tactical items to keep unit costs predictable during the spike:

- Enable prefix/KV caching for the replay-heavy flows you described — we can turn this on for the extension window and it typically reduces token volume by ~30–40% on replay workloads.
- Apply a conservative batching policy (max concurrent requests 8, max batch 64) for the test runner so latency stays stable and cost per 1K tokens is lower.

I’ve included a short success checklist (milestone-checklist.md) we can use to gate the extension:
1) Spike validation (engineering note)
2) Caching enabled and verified
3) SOW amendment executed or credit acceptance confirmed

I can have an engineer join a 30-minute session tomorrow to flip the caching flag and observe.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lewis <emma@clearharbor.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@clearharbor.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 16:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC timeline and usage spike — request to extend runway

Emma — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers inline and then the final ask so we can move quickly: 

1) Overage cap for Option 1: the $5k cap is the maximum you would be billed for overages during the extension; Redwood will not bill beyond $5k for usage in the extension window. That said, the cap is intended to encourage conversion; if you sign the SOW within 30 days of extension end we’ll credit 50% of any billed overage back as a conversion credit (applied to the first invoice).

2) Application of Option 2 credit: we can apply the $15k credit to the pilot bucket immediately so it prevents throttling. It will be reconciled on the first paid invoice once a PO or signed SOW is received within 60 days. If you prefer no PO, we can do an amendment signing via DocuSign (link below) to accept the credit terms and avoid generating a formal PO.

3) Data retention and controls: extending the pilot will not change data retention policies or your configured access controls. This is a tenant-level setting and remains unchanged by a timebox extension or credit issuance. I’ll have security put a two-line confirmation into the SOW amendment for your records.

Final — two concrete options to choose from: 
- Option A (timebox): Free 14-day extension, $5k overage cap, 50% overage credit if SOW signed within 30 days.
- Option B (credit): $15,000 usage credit applied to pilot immediately, reconciled on first invoice once SOW/PO executed within 60 days.

Next steps: pick A or B and we’ll send the amendment (DocuSign) + the milestone checklist. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/CH-POC-2026-05
DocuSign amendment (credit option): https://www.docusign.com/sign/abcdef1234567890

If I don’t hear back by EOD Thursday I’ll provision the free 14-day extension (Option A) so your tests aren’t blocked.

Best,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.com
